risks.note: Manufacturing operations are subject to stringent safety regulations covering process and workforce safety; non-compliance can affect business continuity and reputation.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk across a wide compliance footprint
risks.note: Operations are governed by a wide range of evolving regulations spanning environment, climate change, trade, competition, taxation, and the RBI framework applicable to the NBFC lending business (Aeroflex Finance); non-compliance can affect operational performance and reputation.

Performance is closely linked to global and domestic demand-supply dynamics; movements in stainless steel, polypropylene and other input prices directly affect results, compounded by an energy price shock during the year.

Exposure to physical/environmental damage, trade restrictions from geopolitical tension, and supply disruption; infrastructure constraints across rail, road and port facilities plus dependence on external partners can disrupt operations.

Volatility in financial markets and interest rates can affect the Company's ability to service debt; exposure to currency risk from substantial import/export activity and, through the NBFC lending business, to counterparty credit risk.
Investing in start-ups within disruptive sectors carries the risk of capital loss, and private-market holdings can be illiquid and slow to realise value.

risks.risk: Export and geographic revenue concentration at Aeroflex Neu
risks.note: Exports accounted for ~67% of Aeroflex Neu's revenue during the year, with the business serving over 30 countries, creating exposure to trade and currency conditions in those export markets.

The Board flagged significant uncertainties including geopolitical tension, the West Asia conflict, trade and tariff disputes, inflationary pressure, energy market volatility, commodity price movements and currency fluctuation as ongoing watch-items.

themes.title: General – Industrial Engineering & Mission-Critical Infrastructure Solutions

hero.oneLiner: Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (AEL) is a diversified conglomerate that builds, scales and exits businesses across knowledge-based engineering and advanced manufacturing, tech-enabled industrial and financial services, and a curated start-up investment portfolio.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (AEL) is a diversified conglomerate that builds, scales and exits businesses across knowledge-based engineering and advanced manufacturing, tech-enabled industrial and financial services, and a curated start-up investment portfolio.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: AEL operates through subsidiaries spanning stainless-steel flexible hoses, metal bellows and flow-control solutions (Aeroflex Industries), hydraulic fittings, fluid connectors and flanges (Hyd-Air Engineering), bulk packaging for food, pharma and industrial customers (Aeroflex Neu), and structured finance/SME lending (Aeroflex Finance), serving oil and gas, aerospace, petrochemical, renewable energy, electric mobility and, increasingly, data-centre/AI liquid-cooling infrastructure customers. Alongside these operating businesses, the Group runs a 168-company start-up investment portfolio across 35+ sectors and pursues a 'review and scale' strategy of acquiring undervalued assets, improving their operations, and realising value through strategic exits or IPOs.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Aeroflex Industries Limited — subsidiary: Material subsidiary; 59.84% shareholding as at 31 March 2026
- Aeroflex Neu Limited (formerly Sah Polymers Limited) — subsidiary: Manufacturer/exporter of PP Woven Bags, HDPE Box Bags, FIBCs and BOPP Bags, based in Udaipur, Rajasthan; 55.50% shareholding as at 31 March 2026
- Aeroflex Finance Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; NBFC providing financial services including SME/consumer/education loans; 100% shareholding
- Italica Global FZC, UAE — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary; general trading, import and export activities, headquartered in the UAE; 100% shareholding
- M.R. Organisation Limited — subsidiary: Material subsidiary during FY26 (ISO-certified export house, engineering/last-mile utility services, HQ and manufacturing in Ahmedabad, Gujarat); 51.00% shareholding as at 31 March 2026, but ceased to be a subsidiary with effect from 30 April 2026 pursuant to disinvestment

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Knowledge-based engineering (Aeroflex Industries):** Stainless steel flexible hoses, Metal and miniature bellows, Liquid cooling flow solutions for data centres/AI infrastructure, Skid assemblies and advanced flow control solutions
- **Engineering services (Hyd-Air Engineering):** Hydraulic fittings, Fluid connectors, Flanges
- **Innovative packaging (Aeroflex Neu):** Flexible Intermediate Bulk Container (FIBC) bulk packaging
- **Financial services (Aeroflex Finance):** Structured finance, SME lending

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global data centre liquid cooling market projected to grow from USD 5,655 million (2024) to USD 48,427 million by 2034 (24% CAGR) as rising rack power densities make liquid cooling a core requirement, creating a multi-year demand avenue for precision stainless steel flow solutions, manifolds, skid assemblies and coolant distribution infrastructure that the company is positioning to serve
- Global stainless steel flexible hose market projected to grow from ~USD 2,182 million (CY2025) to ~USD 4,380 million by CY2035 (7.2% CAGR), led by oil and gas (39% of value) plus chemical/petrochemical and power generation (81% combined), driven by migration to corrosion-resistant fluid transfer solutions, industrialisation and infrastructure development
- Global metal bellows market projected to grow from USD 3,012 million (2025) to USD 5,608 million by 2035 (6.4% CAGR), with India growing faster at 7.3% CAGR, as demand from data centres, semiconductors and clean energy layers onto established aerospace and industrial use
- Global FIBC/bulk packaging market projected to grow from ~USD 6.0-6.6 billion (2025) to ~USD 10.4-11.9 billion by 2036 (4.2-6.4% CAGR), with the Indian market growing faster (5.8-8.1% CAGR) on industrialisation, Make in India capacity expansion and export momentum, and a structural shift toward food-grade, certified and recycled-content formats
- Indian tech start-up ecosystem maturing: funding reached USD 9.1 billion in 2025 (+23% YoY) and technology M&A exits more than doubled to 140+ deals in 2025, improving monetisation pathways relevant to AEL's start-up investment portfolio
- Indian macro backdrop of relative resilience — FY26 real GDP growth of 7.7% — though RBI has lowered its FY27 growth forecast to 6.6% (from 6.9%) and raised its inflation projection, citing prolonged West Asia conflict and energy price/supply-chain risk
- Aeroflex Industries signed a long-term contract with a listed U.S. corporation (valued at over USD ~130 billion) to supply liquid cooling solutions for the customer's data centres

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Operate a 'three-engine' portfolio model — a start-up investment portfolio, a value-creation engine that acquires undervalued/high-potential businesses and prepares them for exit, and strategic investments that deepen India's manufacturing capability under Make in India — with deal flow, operational expertise and capital moving across the platform
- Follow a decentralised operating model that lets each subsidiary (Aeroflex Industries, Aeroflex Neu, Aeroflex Finance, and formerly M.R. Organisation) scale independently while benefiting from Group strategic oversight, developing the portfolio into strong, independent entities anchored in governance, transparency and operational resilience
- Optimise value through disciplined, well-timed strategic exits/divestments (as demonstrated by the M.R. Organisation sale), continuing to pursue timely exits alongside identifying new investment opportunities to keep a dynamic portfolio
- Foster the start-up ecosystem by deploying surplus capital into disruptive, high-potential start-ups across a thoughtfully curated, sector-diverse portfolio
- Strengthen core operating businesses through a balanced mix of organic and inorganic growth, capitalising on emerging opportunities in each vertical
- Differentiate through high-quality, customised solutions at the subsidiary level — Aeroflex Industries advancing into liquid cooling, metal/miniature bellows and emerging sectors (fire safety, electric mobility, robotics, semiconductors, aerospace); Aeroflex Neu shifting toward high-compliance food-, pharma- and beverage-grade packaging
- Dividend recommendations are linked to the Company's underlying financial performance rather than a fixed payout formula: the Board recommended a dividend of Re. 0.40 per equity share of face value Rs 2 (20% of face value) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval, on the basis of the Company's performance. No amount was transferred to reserves during FY26.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Aeroflex Industries expanded annual hose manufacturing capacity to 17.5 million metres during FY26 and continued automating its shop floor with the addition of two robotic welding lines, alongside a planned automatic welding station and annealing plant commissioning by December 2026. The subsidiary made a strategic foray into data-centre liquid-cooling infrastructure, entering skid assemblies and advanced flow-control solutions and expanding skid assembly capacity to 6,000 units per annum with plans to scale to 15,000 units by Q2FY27, supported by a long-term supply agreement with a listed U.S. corporation (valued at over USD ~130 billion) for liquid-cooling flow-control components. Following the April 2024 acquisition of Hyd-Air Engineering, its facility underwent significant capability upgrades. At Aeroflex Neu, the Modi Unit received BRCGS Grade A+ certification as part of a strategic shift toward high-compliance food, pharma and beverage packaging.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified three-engine platform (start-up investment portfolio, value-creation/turnaround acquisitions, and strategic manufacturing investments) that reduces reliance on any single business and lets capital and deal flow move across the platform
- Demonstrated value-realisation track record: average 30-35% IRR per annum from successful start-up exits, and the M.R. Organisation divestment delivered a ~3x return (~107% XIRR) to Ingersoll-Rand Industrial US, Inc.
- Global footprint with international offices in the USA, UK, Belgium, Portugal and the UAE and sales touchpoints in 100+ countries
- Long-term contract with a listed U.S. corporation valued at over USD ~130 billion for liquid cooling solutions, evidencing a foothold in the high-growth data centre/AI infrastructure build-out
- Quality certification (BRCGS Grade A+ at Aeroflex Neu's Modi Unit) enabling entry into higher-margin, high-compliance food- and pharma-grade packaging segments

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Safety risk in manufacturing operations — Manufacturing operations are subject to stringent safety regulations covering process and workforce safety; non-compliance can affect business continuity and reputation.
- Regulatory risk across a wide compliance footprint — Operations are governed by a wide range of evolving regulations spanning environment, climate change, trade, competition, taxation, and the RBI framework applicable to the NBFC lending business (Aeroflex Finance); non-compliance can affect operational performance and reputation.
- Commodity price fluctuation — Performance is closely linked to global and domestic demand-supply dynamics; movements in stainless steel, polypropylene and other input prices directly affect results, compounded by an energy price shock during the year.
- Supply chain disruption — Exposure to physical/environmental damage, trade restrictions from geopolitical tension, and supply disruption; infrastructure constraints across rail, road and port facilities plus dependence on external partners can disrupt operations.
- Credit and currency risk — Volatility in financial markets and interest rates can affect the Company's ability to service debt; exposure to currency risk from substantial import/export activity and, through the NBFC lending business, to counterparty credit risk.
- Start-up investment risk — Investing in start-ups within disruptive sectors carries the risk of capital loss, and private-market holdings can be illiquid and slow to realise value.
- Export and geographic revenue concentration at Aeroflex Neu — Exports accounted for ~67% of Aeroflex Neu's revenue during the year, with the business serving over 30 countries, creating exposure to trade and currency conditions in those export markets.
- Macro/geopolitical uncertainty — The Board flagged significant uncertainties including geopolitical tension, the West Asia conflict, trade and tariff disputes, inflationary pressure, energy market volatility, commodity price movements and currency fluctuation as ongoing watch-items.
